title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: main entry point read_lasa_sav(), detects LASA datafile ’re working dispatches correct import/cleaning function automatically: LASA046 files specifically, apply_lasa046_labels() applies SPSS variable- value-labels imports data correctly. current version supports waves: B, C, D, E, 2B, F, G, H, MB, 3B, , J, K future, similar functions built datafiles. importing, can check whether variables matched LASA documentation using lasa_label_report(): returns set “faulty” variables — ones couldn’t matched corresponding documentation — can inspect resolve analysis.
code: library(CleanLASA)  # Import and label a LASA .sav file  # importing the data should generally be in this fomrat: data <- read_lasa_sav("path/to/LASA[wave][file_code].sav")  # Specific examples: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav") # LASA wave B file 046 data <- read_lasa_sav("LASA_data/LASAZ004.sav") # LASA wave Z file 004 data <- read_lasa_sav("Documents/Research/data/LAS2B011.sav") # LASA wave 2B file 011 data <- read_lasa_sav("lasazoa1.sav") # LASA wave Z file oa1 data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAJFI.sav") # LASA wave J file FI # Specifically for LASA046 (Physical Activity), datapath should be in this format: data <- apply_lasa046_labels("path/to/LASA[wave]046.sav")  # Examples data <- apply_lasa046_labels("LASAC046.sav") data <- apply_lasa046_labels("LASMB046.sav") data <- apply_lasa046_labels("LAS3B046.sav") lasa_label_report(data)

title: Apply LASA046 (LAPAQ / Physical Activity) SPSS labels — apply_lasa046_labels
text: data data frame tibble imported LASA046 .sav file (example via haven::read_sav()), containing wave-prefixed variables blphya01, clphya01, etc. wave Character scalar identifying LASA wave, matched case-insensitively. One "B", "C", "D", "E", "2B", "F", "G", "H", "3B", "MB", "", "J", "K". name_corrections Optional named character vector explicit name overrides, used column data exactly case-insensitively match expected LASA046 name (e.g. typo introduced data entry export). Names canonical LASA046 suffixes (without wave prefix), values actual column names found data, example c(lphya08 = "BLPYA08"). correction points column present data recorded "manual_not_found" matching audit rather raising error. to_factor Logical. FALSE (default), categorical variables remain numeric SPSS-style value-label attributes. TRUE, every categorical variable's value labels used factor levels; observed value codebook label retained level (labelled numeric code) rather converted NA. Ignored given variable to_numeric applies instead (see ). to_numeric Logical. FALSE (default), count/continuous variables keep SPSS-style missing-reason value-label attributes. TRUE, every variable whose codebook value labels consist exclusively negative missing-reason codes (e.g. -1, -2, -3) restored ordinary numeric vector: negative values become NA remaining values kept numeric. takes precedence to_factor variables. standardize_names Logical. FALSE (default), original column names data left unchanged. TRUE, every successfully matched LASA046 column renamed canonical lowercase documentation name, blphya01, clphya26, klphya50. Renaming happens variables matched, affect matching decisions; function stops informative error renaming create duplicate column names.

title: Apply LASA046 (LAPAQ / Physical Activity) SPSS labels — apply_lasa046_labels
text: LASA046 variable names, wording, value codings change across waves (example, sport-type coding scheme redesigned starting wave H, several items exist subset waves). wave must supplied explicitly several waves share variable-name prefix ("b" B, 2B, 3B, MB) use different labels/codings. Column matching tries, order: (1) explicit override name_corrections, (2) exact (case-sensitive) name match, (3) case-insensitive name match. LASA046 variable matched left unlabelled recorded "found" matching audit rather raising error, since every wave's file contains every variable. name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names part parameter contract shared every apply_*_labels() function package (see header comment lasa_io.R). read_lasa_sav() forwards four arguments automatically dispatching function, can supplied either directly apply_lasa046_labels() read_lasa_sav() – forms behave identically.

title: Search the LASA topic table — lasa_topics
text: Topic, theme, subtheme matching case-insensitive. Incomplete names small typographical errors accepted fuzzy_match = TRUE. Supplying theme searches main LASA themes subthemes. LASA topics documented several related file codes one row topic table, main file, telephone-interview version, longitudinally cleaned version. LASA site's label row spells (example "Self-report chronic diseases - tel. proxy - tel. respondent"), file code returned part label describes (e.g. "Self-report chronic diseases - tel. proxy" proxy-interview file code) rather full combined label repeated every code. Splitting prefers row's column layout falls back LASA file-code numbering convention (0/1 = main face--face file, 2/3 = processed derived file, 4/5 = longitudinally cleaned revised file, 6 = telephone interview proxy, 7 = telephone interview respondent); single file code covers several qualifiers (nothing disambiguate), full descriptive list dropped favor plain base topic name. small number rows need information present compact topic-table text - lives file code's variable-information PDF, topic page's prose, specific domain knowledge - scraper can derive table alone. rows carry curated, documented correction (see data-raw/lasa_topic_overrides.R package source full list reasoning behind one). curation applied every time table built, independently refresh.

Forwarded selected file-specific label function. TRUE, count/continuous variables (whose codebook value labels negative missing-reason codes) restored plain numeric, negative codes converted NA. Takes precedence to_factor variables. standardize_names Logical, default FALSE. Forwarded selected file-specific label function. TRUE, every successfully matched column renamed canonical lowercase LASA documentation name (e.g. blphya01). ... title: Read and label a LASA SPSS data file — read_lasa_sav
text: dispatcher follows LASA filename convention: regular single-letter waves: LASA[wave][file_code].SAV, e.g. LASAE046.SAV; waves 2B, 3B, 4B, MB: LAS[wave][file_code].SAV, e.g. LAS3B046.SAV; information stored across waves: wave code Z, e.g. LASAZ004.SAV; file codes contain 2 3 alphanumeric characters interpreted case-insensitively. File-specific label functions selected convention. file code starts number, expected function apply_lasa[file_code]_labels(); example, file 046 maps apply_lasa046_labels() file 004 maps apply_lasa004_labels(). file code starts letter, expected function apply_lasa_[file_code]_labels(); example, FI maps apply_lasa_fi_labels(). OA files oa1, oa2, oa3 hard-coded family map apply_lasa_oa_labels(). Every apply_*_labels() function package shares parameter contract: data, wave- /file-code-identifying argument, four reshaping arguments documented (name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names; see apply_lasa046_labels() canonical implementation). read_lasa_sav() declares four reshaping arguments explicitly, defaults shown , callers can discover use without needing know file-specific function ultimately dispatched . selected function must already available package namespace current R session. read_lasa_sav() inspects function's formal arguments (via formals()) : always supplies data; supplies wave /file_code function declares ; supplies name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names function declares , otherwise warns – rather silently ignoring request – caller supplied non-default value one ; forwards named arguments ... unchanged, file-specific parameters fall outside shared contract. permits shared implementations future apply_lasa_oa_labels(data, file_code, name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names, ...) coexist wave-aware ones apply_lasa046_labels(data, wave, name_corrections, to_factor, to_numeric, standardize_names). labelling, generic provenance attributes attached: "LASA_wave", "LASA_file_code", "LASA_source_file", "LASA_label_function". File-specific functions attach variable-name matching audit generic "label_report" attribute; retrieve lasa_label_report().

title: Read and label a LASA SPSS data file — read_lasa_sav
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Automatically dispatches to apply_lasa046_labels() dat_e <- read_lasa_sav("LASAE046.SAV")  # Also dispatches to apply_lasa046_labels(), with wave = "3B" dat_3b <- read_lasa_sav("LAS3B046.SAV")  # The four shared reshaping arguments are available directly on # read_lasa_sav(), without needing to know they live on # apply_lasa046_labels() specifically: dat_h <- read_lasa_sav(   "LASAH046.SAV",   to_factor = TRUE,   to_numeric = TRUE,   standardize_names = TRUE )  # Manually correct a mistyped column name: dat_b <- read_lasa_sav(   "LASAB046.SAV",   name_corrections = c(lphya08 = "BLPYA08") )  # Dispatches to apply_lasa004_labels() once that function exists dat_z004 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAZ004.SAV")  # Both dispatch to apply_lasa_oa_labels() once that function exists oa1 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAzoa1.sav") oa2 <- read_lasa_sav("LASAzoa2.sav") } # }
